name: liquid C2H6 at 94 K (an estimated index)
paper: the estimate's inputs: Loria, Ann. Phys. 334 (1909) 605, Table IX, with refractiveindex.info's refit of a, for C2H6's gas dispersion; D. Bücker and W. Wagner, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 35 (2006) 205, DOI 10.1063/1.1859286, for the liquid's density
source: a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate, not a measurement (decision-r08-t5d ruling 5's method, as for the ices): the molar refraction of C2H6 from its gas dispersion as stated at 273.15 K and 101325 Pa (view/atmosphere/rayleigh.ts's row, Z = 0.99897), measured over 523–667.7 nm and extrapolated beyond, with no increment, since the liquid is molecular and non-polar, over the saturated liquid's molar volume at 94 K, 46.436 cm³ mol⁻¹ (21.53485 mol/l from the NIST Chemistry WebBook, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C74840&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=95&TLow=94&TInc=1&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 32926b1df39c2492c1da071470aefa212e1c80dbb7bcd887991daecc4704bc2c, fetched 2026-10-14). It gives 1.4157 at 380 nm, 1.4008 at 550 nm and 1.3940 at 780 nm. No open measurement of liquid ethane's visible optical constants was found (R08.T5.g's search, 2026-10-14: refractiveindex.info, which holds Loria's gas only; the NIST Chemistry WebBook; Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv, NASA's NTRS, Europe PMC and Google Scholar, for its refractive index or visible absorption, pure or in Titan's methane–ethane–nitrogen mixtures). Three measurements are closed: Badoz et al. 1992 (Rev. Sci. Instrum. 63, 2967, DOI 10.1063/1.1142594), a cryogenic refractometer at 670 nm for liquid methane, ethane and nitrogen and their mixtures; Sliwinski 1969 (Z. Phys. Chem. 63, 263, DOI 10.1524/zpch.1969.63.5_6.263), the Lorentz–Lorenz function of liquid ethane; and Lopez-Calvo and Manzanares 2008 (J. Phys. Chem. A 112, 1730, DOI 10.1021/jp076843v), whose abstract reports the C–H overtone Δv = 6 of liquid ethane at 100 K, past 14,000 cm⁻¹, in the red. Burton's thesis (University of British Columbia, DOI 10.14288/1.0084897, CC BY; its abstract, through OpenAlex) gives ethane's measured Lorentz–Lorenz function at 632.8 nm, 0.3794 ± 0.0003 cm³ g⁻¹, constant within 0.5% over 1–200 amagat: extrapolated to the liquid's density, about 483 amagat, n = 1.4061, 0.0086 above this estimate there, since Loria's molar refraction runs lower (R08.T5.g's deferred finding). The method's checks on measured liquids, each above the measurement: liquid Ar at 90 K against Sinnock and Smith 1969 (Phys. Rev. 181, 1297), +0.0023 at 546.1 nm; liquid N2 at 77.32 K against Augustin 1915 (Ann. Phys. 351, 419), +0.0019 at 546.1 nm; liquid CH4 at 90.694 K against Martonchik and Orton 1994's 90 K (Appl. Opt. 33, 8306), +0.0074 at 583.1 nm; liquid NH3 at 239.80 K against Wong and Anderson 1972 (J. Opt. Soc. Am. 62, 219), +0.0057 at 632.8 nm (their molar densities: Ar https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C7440371&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=91&TLow=90&TInc=1&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 99a13ee0ffe92c6576e99fdd90c761427cb85a322e1347ce839fcbb6e9873a73, fetched 2026-10-14; CH4 https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C74828&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=91&TLow=90&TInc=1&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 5b8e05aee257ebaf342dfce6836443eb61dc6dbe5968aa0aafd3ae4164525560, fetched 2026-10-14; N2 https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C7727379&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=77.355&TLow=77&TInc=0.355&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 5022a4ab7b30bde7942baf2b8c13fbcef6b6b9bf3319ae8f0fa5b001f216dad7, fetched 2026-10-14; NH3 https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C7664417&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=240&TLow=239.8&TInc=0.2&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 0a64ea66717939006d109c2f3707e652c4963f336ba1238c5fbb6d656d73a42c, fetched 2026-10-14). k = 0: no open measurement of liquid ethane's visible absorption was found, and its weak C–H overtones in the red are not drawn
licence: estimated values from cited constants: a gas dispersion and a density from the NIST Chemistry WebBook (NIST Standard Reference Data, cited); no data set is copied
reduction: n = √((1 + 2x) ÷ (1 − x)), with x the gas's molar refraction over the liquid's molar volume, evaluated on 380–780 nm every 5 nm to six significant figures; k = 0. The method runs 0.0019 to 0.0074 high on the four measured liquids, so ethane's n is presumably as high, while Burton's function would raise it
standIn: a non-absorbing liquid whose real index is a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate from the gas's dispersion at the liquid's density, since no open visible optical constants of liquid C2H6 were found: 1.416 at 380 nm, 1.401 at 550 nm and 1.394 at 780 nm
